question.text: A steel wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi>S</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> and a copper wire of length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>Y</mi><mi mathvariant="italic">C</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math> , both of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math> are connected end to end. When stretched by a load, the net elongation is found to be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mm</mi></math>. The load applied, in Newton, will be: (Given <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>π</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mn>22</mn><mn>7</mn></mfrac></math>)

solution.text:
When two wires are connected end to end, the tension in them will be same.

Change in length using Hooke's law can be found as,

Y=FlA∆l⇒Δl=FlAY

Total change in length can be written as,

Δl=Δl1+Δl2   

⇒Δl=Fl1 A1Y1+Fl2 A2Y2

⇒F=Δll1 A1Y1+l2 A2Y2=1.4×10-33.2π1.4×10-32×2.0×1011+4.4π1.4×10-32×1.1×1011⇒F=1.54×102=154 N
